I do not have the same beliefs you do to Spirituality and Magic. I don't believe they exist and as an engineer, I may place you on the same par as your rock musicians. HOWEVER, I do believe that a lot of our great art comes from people who believe in the occult. You may consider me a bit of a mindless automoton with no imagination, and you'd probably be mostly right (I have no imagination) but by my own perspective I would consider you a bit crazy for believing in spiritual stuff.

You are what we refer to as a "materialist." Once you realize that you cannot solve the hard problem of consciousness through a materialist perspective, you will begin to understand what spirituality is and why it is so much more fundamental to philosophical understanding than objective observation.

Materialists tend to think that consciousness "comes from the brain," which is to say that subjectivity is a property of a specific organization of matter. If you analyze this claim, you find that it is as ridiculous and irrational as you think spiritualists are. If the brain is what creates consciousness (meaning that where there is no brain, there is no consciousness), then as an engineer, why don't you go ahead and draw me up a blueprint for the simplest possible brain that is conscious, and then explain to me the physical reason why it ceases to be conscious when you remove just one single cell from it. Is that not a ridiculous suggestion? The idea that awareness itself simply magically pops into and out of existence when atoms are arranged in a certain way?

You'll find that it makes more sense that consciousness exists in all holistic systems (particles, atoms, molecules, cells, organisms) and that the complexity of the system equals the complexity of the consciousness. The consciousness of a human body (brain) is the integrated consciousness of all of its constituent particles. That's how the mind can arise -- it is built from tiny mind blocks in the same way that the body is built from tiny body blocks.

Once you make that philosophical leap, it's not hard to understand why magic and spirituality make sense. If consciousness is everywhere and universally connected at a sub-particle level, then it must have mechanistic properties that can be operated on. Magic is the study and practice of how to do this.

To understand magic, first understand subjectivity. Ponder how bizarre it is that you are aware of anything at all. Why would that be? Why does having a brain mean that you can actually feel and experience? How does experience come from matter? If you think you have an answer to this question, you're wrong. No one does. That's why it's called the "hard" problem of consciousness.

I've long been interested in space and marine colonization and was, for many years, president of a once large space advocacy group called the First Millennial Foundation/Living Universe Foundation. It was formed to pursue the space development vision of futurist Marshal Savage, described in his book The Millennial Project.

But space and marine development have been heavily infiltrated by Randian Libertarians dreaming of Galt's Gulch who simply ruin everything they get involved in. They have no concept of social responsibility, cooperation, or community. Everything is a f-ing ape troop fight for dominance or a Darwinian competition. And then there are all the Newage fanatics and X-Files conspiracy kooks forever drawn to the subjects of space, ecology, and intentional community. I kid you not, we used to have to repeatedly deal with this guy who's whole motivation for marine development was that he wanted to build places at sea where he could go have sex with dolphins.

Social media has also taken a toll on the space advocacy movement. It's made it impossible for groups to communicate and organize coherently because people now go ape every time you put more than a paragraph of text in their face. Social media induces a rhythm to the browsing of information, producing a kind of hypnogogic state, and anything that interrupts that rhythm by actually compelling one to think triggers a road-rage-like response akin to someone caught in a traffic jam. So it's impossible to get down to the details of planning anything. I was constantly getting alternately criticized for lack of plans then attacked for presenting plans because I expected people to read. Everything has to be reduced to a Bush-style executive summary, YouTube video, or comic book form. I kept trying to devise and propose projects to motivate people's involvement but even getting down to Boy Scout level stuff was too much for the average space enthusiast, who apparently hasn't so much as held a hammer in their hands in decades. Year after year the space advocacy community--if not American society in general--started looking more and more like the sad ending of Mondo Cane. Eventually I just gave up.

I still pursue ideas for an Open Space movement, like the telebase concept I've talked about here in the past. Space advocacy may be hopeless, but I see some hope in the Maker community. But it still remains impossible to communicate with this society without a big media budget capable of putting everything in pictures. The written word is dead. I am increasingly of the opinion that we've likely already relegated the stars to future artilects and will end up just like those cargo cultists in New Guinea, sitting in the dirt and staring at the sky.
